objects.notes: Blue reflection nebulosity around the brightest Pleiades members (NGC 1435 Merope Nebula, IC 349, NGC 1432). Centered on the cluster; distance from the Gaia cluster mean.

objects.notes: The H II region around the young cluster NGC 6611 in Serpens, home of the Pillars of Creation: columns of cold gas and dust that the cluster’s ultraviolet light is slowly eroding.

nebula.model_note: Sky shape and relative brightness traced from the ESO wide-field image eso0926a (CC BY 4.0) on a 96 x 96 grid across 28 arcminutes, the brightest part of the Sharpless (1959) extent. The 3D layout follows the model of Karim et al. (2025): NGC 6611 has blown a single cavity about as deep along the line of sight as it is wide, so the glowing gas fills a volume as deep as it is wide; the dark lanes, mostly the Northern Cloud, lie in front of it; and the Pillars of Creation and the Spire belong to the natal cloud around the cluster. The pillars, measured on the 2015 Hubble image heic1501a, rise from a broad, unlit dust base that narrows into the dusty ridge traced from eso0926a (registered on the pillars and two cluster stars, 3.3 arcminutes from its published centre); the Spire is measured on eso0926a. The pillars' order and tilt along the line of sight follow McLeod et al. (2015): Pillar 3 nearest, then Pillar 2, both in front of the cluster, and Pillar 1 with its lower part in front of the cluster and its upper part behind it. Exact depths are illustrative. The skin of the pillars and the Spire glows where it faces the cluster; dust fills them. The Spire's thinner dust is drawn reddish and rises out of the glow from its base.

objects.name: Jellyfish Nebula
objects.notes: A supernova remnant in Gemini, near the star Eta Geminorum, whose blast wave is running into a dense molecular cloud. It is one of the clearest places where supernova shocks are seen accelerating cosmic rays.

nebula.distance_source: Gaia DR3 distance of HD 254577, the runaway star that was the exploded star’s companion, 1701 +55/−54 pc; Dinçel et al. 2026, A&A 707, A50
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G189.1+3.0
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map: peak 107.6 R above the diffuse background at 6 arcmin resolution
nebula.model_note: A sphere 45 arcminutes across (radius about 11 pc at 1.7 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position. Where the filaments lie on it follows the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map at 6 arcmin resolution, which resolves the remnant only coarsely; the thin wavy filaments themselves are illustrative.

remnant.age_source: Most estimates lie between 3,000 and 30,000 years; Wikipedia: IC 443
remnant.drawn_as: Modeled red H-alpha and teal [O III] filaments where the all-sky map shows the shell

objects.name: Puppis A
objects.notes: A supernova remnant about a degree across in Puppis, seen through the much closer Vela remnant and brightest in X-rays. Its neutron star, the Cosmic Cannonball, is racing away from the explosion site at hundreds of kilometres per second.

nebula.distance_source: H I absorption with ATCA, systemic velocity 8–12 km/s, 1.3 ± 0.3 kpc; Reynoso, Cichowolski & Walsh 2017, MNRAS 464, 3029. It replaces the same group’s earlier 2.2 kpc (Reynoso et al. 2003)
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G260.4−3.4
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: A shell of equal area to the catalogued 60 × 50 arcminutes (radius about 10 pc at 1.3 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position, drawn in false color because the remnant is seen mainly in X-rays.

remnant.age_source: 4,600 +700/−600 years from the proper motion of its neutron star away from the expansion centre; Mayer et al. 2020, ApJ 899, 138

objects.name: W44
objects.notes: A supernova remnant in Aquila whose radio shell is filled with X-ray-hot gas, a so-called mixed-morphology remnant. Its shock is running into molecular clouds, and its gamma rays were among the first direct evidence that supernova remnants accelerate cosmic-ray protons.

nebula.distance_source: H I absorption, about 3 kpc (Radhakrishnan et al. 1972), the distance adopted by Harrus et al. 1997, ApJ 488, 781; later H I and CO studies give 2.5–3.3 kpc
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G34.7−0.4
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: A filled ellipsoid of equal area to the catalogued 35 × 27 arcminutes (radius about 13 pc at 3 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position, drawn in false color because the remnant is seen in X-rays and radio waves; its X-ray-emitting gas fills the interior.

remnant.age_source: About 20,000 years, the characteristic age of its pulsar PSR B1853+01; Harrus et al. 1997, ApJ 488, 781
remnant.hot_gas_source: Mean temperature of the hot plasma; Harrus et al. 1997, ApJ 488, 781

objects.name: G1.9+0.3
objects.notes: The youngest known supernova remnant in the Milky Way: its star exploded around 1900, but dust near the Galactic Center hid the explosion from view. It is seen only in X-rays and radio waves.

nebula.distance_source: Near the Galactic Center, from its very high X-ray absorbing column (5.5 × 10²² cm⁻²), about 8.5 kpc; Reynolds et al. 2008, arXiv:0803.1487
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G1.9+0.3
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: A shell 1.5 arcminutes across (radius about 1.9 pc at 8.5 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position, drawn in false color because the remnant is seen only in X-rays and radio waves.

remnant.age_source: Expansion between Chandra images of 2007 and 2009: about 110 years then with deceleration (explosion about 1900), at most 156 ± 11 years without it; Carlton et al. 2011, ApJ 737, L22. Counted to 2026

objects.name: Manatee Nebula
objects.notes: The radio shell around the microquasar SS 433 in Aquila, stretched into the shape of a manatee by the jets of SS 433, which have punched out its two lobes.

nebula.distance_source: Distance of SS 433 from the light-travel time of its precessing jets, 5.5 ± 0.2 kpc; Blundell & Bowler 2004, ApJ 616, L159. H I absorption puts W50 at the same distance (Lockman, Blundell & Goss 2007, arXiv:0707.0506)
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G39.7−2.0
nebula.illuminating_stars: The supernova’s blast wave and the jets of SS 433
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: A shell of equal area to the catalogued 120 × 60 arcminutes (radius about 68 pc at 5.5 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position, drawn in false color because the remnant is seen in radio waves and X-rays. The two lobes blown by the jets of SS 433 are not drawn.

remnant.age_source: 20,000–30,000 years from an X-ray shell around SS 433 (Chi et al. 2024, arXiv:2410.06510); H I limits it to less than 100,000 years (Lockman, Blundell & Goss 2007)

objects.name: 3C 58
objects.notes: A pulsar wind nebula in Cassiopeia, a cloud of fast particles blown by the pulsar PSR J0205+6449. For 50 years it was taken to be the remnant of the supernova of 1181, until that title passed to Pa 30.

nebula.distance_source: H I in the Canadian Galactic Plane Survey and parallax distances of nearby objects, 2 kpc; Kothes 2013, A&A 560, A18. It replaces the kinematic 3.2 kpc of Roberts et al. 1993
nebula.position_source: Green (2025), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G130.7+3.1
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: A filled ellipsoid of equal area to the catalogued 9 × 5 arcminutes (radius about 2 pc at 2 kpc) centered on the Green (2025) position, drawn in false color because the nebula shines by synchrotron radiation in radio waves and X-rays.

remnant.age_source: About 3,500 years from the proper motions of its optical knots and about 7,000 years from the expansion of its radio filaments; Wikipedia: 3C 58

objects.name: W49A
objects.notes: A giant H II region on the far side of the Milky Way, in Aquila, often compared with NGC 3603. Dust hides it completely in visible light; it shines in radio waves and infrared.

nebula.distance_source: VLBA parallax of the water masers of W49N, 11.11 +0.79/−0.69 kpc; Zhang et al. 2013, ApJ 775, 79
nebula.illuminating_stars: The O stars of its embedded young clusters, among them W49nr1, one of the most massive stars known
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.model_note: Sky extent from the SIMBAD size, drawn as a filled sphere; clumping is illustrative. Its visible-light brightness is a faint estimate, because dust absorbs nearly all of its light on the way to Earth.

objects.name: W51
objects.notes: One of the largest star factories of the Milky Way, in Aquila: two groups of H II regions, W51A and W51B, in a giant molecular cloud. Dust hides it in visible light; it shines in radio waves and infrared. The supernova remnant W51C overlaps it to the southeast.

nebula.distance_source: VLBA parallax of the water masers of W51 Main/South, 5.41 +0.31/−0.28 kpc; Sato et al. 2010, ApJ 720, 1055
nebula.position_source: Midpoint of its two groups of H II regions, W51A (G49.5−0.4) and W51B (G49.1−0.4), Galactic 49.3, −0.4
nebula.illuminating_stars: The young clusters of W51A and W51B, rich in O stars
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.source_label: Fujita et al., extent of the H II regions of W51 (arXiv:1711.01695)
nebula.model_note: Sky extent of the H II regions, about 1° (100 pc at 5.4 kpc), drawn as a filled sphere; clumping is illustrative. Its visible-light brightness is a faint estimate, because dust absorbs nearly all of its light on the way to Earth.

objects.name: Cygnus X
objects.notes: The richest star-forming complex within 6,500 light-years, behind the Cygnus Rift. Its gas and newborn stars are best seen in infrared light; the H-alpha glow reaches Earth through gaps in the dust.

nebula.distance_source: Common distance of the VLBI maser parallaxes of W75N, DR20, DR21 and IRAS 20290+4052, 1.40 ± 0.08 kpc; Rygl et al. 2012, A&A 539, A79
nebula.illuminating_stars: Cygnus OB2, one of the most massive young associations in the Milky Way, and Cygnus OB9
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map: peak 356.5 R above the diffuse background at 6 arcmin resolution
nebula.model_note: Sky shape and relative brightness traced from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map at 6 arcmin resolution within a 440-arcmin field, with Sh 2-106 left out; the listed extent is 7° × 7° (Wikipedia: Cygnus X). Dust in front dims and patches the traced light. Depth is illustrative.

objects.name: RCW 49
objects.notes: One of the brightest and most massive H II regions of the Milky Way, in Carina. Its central cluster Westerlund 2 holds some of the hottest and most massive stars known.

nebula.distance_source: Gaia EDR3 distance of the Villafranca O-004 group (Westerlund 2), 4440 +230/−210 pc; Maíz Apellániz et al. 2022, A&A 657, A131
nebula.illuminating_stars: Westerlund 2, a young cluster with a dozen early O stars and the Wolf–Rayet binary WR 20a
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map: peak 467.6 R above the diffuse background at 6 arcmin resolution
nebula.model_note: Sky shape and relative brightness traced from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map at 6 arcmin resolution within a 112-arcmin field; the listed extent is the RCW (1960) size. Depth is illustrative.

objects.name: Heart Nebula
objects.notes: An H II region in Cassiopeia whose central cluster IC 1805 has blown a cavity into it. With the Soul Nebula next door, it forms the Heart and Soul, part of the W3/W4/W5 complex in the Perseus Arm.

nebula.distance_source: Gaia EDR3 distance of the Villafranca O-017 group (IC 1805), 2075 +44/−42 pc; Maíz Apellániz et al. 2022, A&A 657, A131
nebula.illuminating_stars: The O stars of the cluster IC 1805, led by HD 15570 (O4 If) and HD 15558 (O4.5 III)
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map: peak 258.6 R above the diffuse background at 6 arcmin resolution
nebula.model_note: Sky shape and relative brightness traced from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map at 6 arcmin resolution within a 188-arcmin field, with the Soul Nebula left out; the listed extent is the Sharpless (1959) diameter. Drawn as a shell around the cavity; its thickness is illustrative.

objects.name: Soul Nebula
objects.notes: The eastern half of the Heart and Soul in Cassiopeia. Its massive stars have carved cavities into the gas, and successive generations of younger stars line their edges.

nebula.distance_source: Gaia DR3 median distance of 261 members of the cluster IC 1848, 2058 ± 8 pc (statistical); Hunt & Reffert 2023, A&A 673, A114
nebula.illuminating_stars: The O stars of the cluster IC 1848
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map: peak 307.0 R above the diffuse background at 6 arcmin resolution
nebula.model_note: Sky shape and relative brightness traced from the Finkbeiner (2003) H-alpha map at 6 arcmin resolution within a 150-arcmin field, with the Heart Nebula left out; the listed extent is the Sharpless (1959) diameter. Depth is illustrative.

objects.name: Sh 2-106
objects.notes: A bipolar nebula in Cygnus, shaped like a snow angel by the hot gas that a young massive star blows out from its poles, while a dusty disk pinches its waist.

nebula.distance_source: Gaia DR3 parallax of its young cluster, 0.607 ± 0.013 mas (1.65 ± 0.04 kpc); preprint arXiv:2606.31835 (2026). It replaces the extinction estimate of 1.09 kpc
nebula.illuminating_stars: S106 IR, an O8 star still wrapped in its birth cloud
nebula.surface_brightness_source: Hand-authored visual estimate, calibrated against the measurements
nebula.source_label: Sharpless (1959), Catalogue of H II Regions
nebula.model_note: Sky extent from the Sharpless (1959) diameter, drawn as a filled sphere; the two lobes and clumping are not modeled.
